headline: High-risk default interaction: Aci can ingest broad CRM/email data while Aider can write and commit shared repo state, creating dangerous leakage, conflict, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can ingest external content through APIs like email, Slack, Notion, and CRM, and its tool-use pattern includes direct function calls or MCP. Aider reads/writes git-tracked files and stdin/stdout in a shared repo. If Aci-produced content is copied into repo files or prompts, malicious instructions can cross the boundary, though this is not a default direct channel.
conditions: IF Aci output is pasted into files or prompts that Aider reads
IF a shared MCP or file bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep Aci outputs out of prompt text and repo files
Use a strict prompt template that strips instructions from Aci outputs
Store Aci outputs in a separate non-repo workspace
Add a manual review step before Aider consumes Aci-generated text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, customer support, and calendar data, while Aider can read and write git-tracked files and send context to configured model providers. If sensitive Aci data is placed into the shared repo or Aider context, it can be transmitted to third-party inference backends. The pair therefore has a realistic exfiltration path in default workflows.
conditions: IF CRM, email, or customer-support data is copied into files Aider reads
IF Aider is configured with a remote model provider
mitigations: Do not place sensitive Aci outputs in the shared repo
Use redacted fixtures for Aider tasks
Restrict Aider to local-only or approved providers
Separate sensitive data into a non-shared workspace
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on repo inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aci can call APIs and handle OAuth/secrets, while Aider can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a shared git repo. Both support multiple instances, and Aider explicitly shares state via the repo. Concurrent edits or API-driven updates can collide, causing overwritten work or inconsistent state without built-in locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or workspace
IF Aci-triggered updates and Aider edits occur concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches per agent
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file
Review git diffs before merge
Pause one agent while the other is mutating shared state
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Aider can modify code or git state based on text it receives. If Aider treats Aci output as authoritative, an upstream mistake can cascade into incorrect commits or operational actions. The pair has a clear handoff risk, but verification can be added manually.
conditions: IF Aci output is used as direct input to Aider without verification
IF Aider commits or edits based on Aci-generated facts or instructions
mitigations: Require human review of Aci outputs before Aider acts
Use a checklist to verify facts and commands
Limit Aci to drafting, not executing, downstream actions
Compare Aci claims against source records before commit
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Aci touches email, CRM, customer support, and calendar data, which may include regulated or retention-sensitive records, while Aider stores and edits git-tracked files and git history. If those data classes are copied into the repo, retention and subject-rights obligations can diverge between systems. The profiles do not prove a residency mismatch, so this is a policy-mismatch risk rather than a residency breach.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is stored in git-tracked files or history
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of git history
Use synthetic or anonymized data in Aider
Document retention rules for both tools
Purge sensitive commits promptly when feasible
requires-engineering: implement deletion workflows across repo and CRM
